reviews.reason: The argument combines a geometric line-bundle problem with polynomial growth and a controlled local-duality obstruction. Choosing a single section that converts all tensor powers into linear growth is a substantive H2 step after the declared local algebra, rather than a direct application of a Picard restriction theorem.
reviews.core_assessment: Encode a line bundle trivial modulo f as an invertible coherent triple, and use the retained Hilbert-triple and positivity arguments to obtain a nonnegative polynomial detecting its tensor powers. Use local duality and the depth hypotheses to confine the obstruction module to one-dimensional support, then choose a section and derive a linear bound incompatible with nonzero even polynomial growth.
reviews.prerequisite_assessment: Local cohomology and normalized dualizing complexes, Matlis duality, depth/support inequalities, Hilbert–Samuel growth in dimension one, existence of a nonvanishing section on finitely many points of a quasi-affine scheme, and catenary S2 dimension theory. Coherent triples and their polynomial/positivity lemmas are retained local proof.

This is an initial targeted assessment, not an independently confirmed clearance.

editorial_notes: In the local-duality diagram the printed bound adds the length of the entire Ext^-2(A/fA,omega) module, which may have one-dimensional support and infinite length. The finite term needed by the diagram is the image of the lower horizontal arrow; this image is zero because depth(A)>=3 gives Ext^-2(A,omega)=0. Thus the same diagram bounds the upper image by the finite-length cokernel of t_0, and the subsequent Hilbert–Samuel linear-growth argument applies. The original wording is retained and this precise missing-image qualification is disclosed.

Only the stated depth/dimension hypotheses are assumed; no regularity or complete-intersection assumption is silently added. The separate preceding torsion-freeness corollary is uncounted supporting material.
